title: Cut the two redundant coverage builds out of /coverage-loop
description:
Every iteration of /coverage-loop runs the instrumented build two more times than it needs to, and tools/coverage.sh wipes and rebuilds .coverage-build/<submodule>/ on every invocation, so each one is a full rebuild.

First: Stage 5 measures twice. verifier.md step 1 runs ./tools/coverage.sh --no-notify <submodule>, then coverage-loop.md line 139 re-dispatches coverage-runner, which runs the identical command against a tree nothing touched in between.

Second: Stage 1 re-measures an untouched tree. On iterations after the first, nothing changes between Stage 5 measuring and the next Stage 1 measuring again.

Fix both: have the verifier emit coverage-runner's report block (STATUS / pct / baseline / BASELINE_MOVED) from the run it already did and delete the Stage 5 re-dispatch; and have Stage 1 measure only on iteration 1, with later iterations reading the previous entry's coverage value out of loop-log.json.
design: Folding the measurement into the verifier does not violate the never-grade-your-own-work rule: the verifier is read-only and authored nothing in the wave. A reviewer who reproduced the gate green from a clean state is stronger evidence than a separate agent's number, not weaker. This is the largest wall-clock win available in the harness and is most of why a 3-iteration cap feels expensive.
acceptance_criteria: One gate run per iteration boundary instead of three. Stage 5 dispatches the verifier only. Stage 1 reads loop-log on iterations 2 and 3.

title: Build the /coverage-loop pipeline: command, agents, skills, hooks
description: Replace ad-hoc skill invocation with an explicit orchestrated loop. A /coverage-loop slash command drives five scoped subagents (coverage-runner, triager, test-writer, refactorer, verifier) that follow four skills (coverage, triage, testing, refactor). Skills hold domain procedure, agents hold execution context and tool allowlists, the command holds the loop. Hooks in .claude/settings.json enforce the branch policy and syntax-check test edits.
design: Adapted to this repo rather than the generic design: tools/coverage.sh and tools/triage.sh are the runner and classifier, coverage/<name>.triage.json is the existing A/B/C contract so the triager selects from it rather than re-deriving it, the loop threshold is measured against the addressable ceiling not raw coverage, and test work happens on a branch inside the submodule (two PRs per the branch policy).
acceptance_criteria: /coverage-loop exists and runs; five agent definitions with scoped tools; testing and refactor skills written; hooks wired and executable; all four repos' branch policy respected by the loop.

title: Apply the branch policy to the three subrepos
description: With the policy established in the root repo, apply it to helios, hills, and hyperspace: enable GitHub branch protection on each master (require a PR, no direct pushes), and add a short AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md pointer in each so an agent working inside a submodule sees the rule without reading the superproject. Requires gh auth.

title: Regenerate the stale helios coverage baseline and triage data
description: coverage/helios.json and coverage/helios.triage.json were measured against the deleted fork's Metal-ported code. The re-forked helios is at v2.1.1, pre-Metal, so both files describe code that no longer exists and the ratchet gate would compare against a meaningless baseline. Re-run ./tools/coverage.sh helios and ./tools/triage.sh helios against the new tree and commit fresh data.

title: Rewrite branch policy and re-pin helios to the re-forked remote
description: The root repo's branch policy (CLAUDE.md:74) contradicts its own session-completion checklist, which ends at 'git push' rather than at an opened PR. AGENTS.md omits the branch rule entirely. Separately, the helios fork was deleted and re-forked, leaving the submodule pinned to a dangling SHA. Establish the new process in the root repo and re-pin helios, all via a feature branch and PR.

title: Decide how the superproject gets a server-enforced review gate
description:
This is a decision, not an implementation, and it blocks any automated ship harness.

Verified current state of the four repos. helios, hills and hyperspace are public forks with no branch protection -- the protection endpoint returns 404 branch not protected and rulesets is empty, both fixable with a single gh api PUT. fiazsami/screen-savers is a private repo on a free plan, where both the branch-protection and the rulesets endpoints return 403 upgrade to GitHub Pro or make this repository public. There is no configuration that puts protection on the superproject default branch as things stand.

So the choice is: make screen-savers public, pay for Pro, or accept that nothing server-side gates the superproject merge and that a script's own polling is the entire gate. The third is defensible, but only if the polling then fails closed on a missing check rather than treating absent as passed -- because it becomes load-bearing rather than belt-and-braces.

There is a second half to the decision, which matters more than strict-versus-permissive: what artifact constitutes review. A check-run conclusion, a reviewDecision, or a human. Only the first can work unattended, and only if the review is exposed as a check run under an exact known name. A required approving review instead parks mergeStateStatus at BLOCKED -- a bot review generally does not satisfy it and an author cannot approve their own PR -- so every PR would burn its full timeout and report a failure. Answer that first; strict versus permissive follows from it.

Worth noting the asymmetry: the three repos that can be protected are the ones whose PRs carry the actual code and merge first. The one that cannot carries only pointers and baselines. That is the more forgiving way round, and it is luck rather than design.
design: Sources: harness-build-instructions-review.md sections 2.1 through 2.4 and ship-harness-audit.md sections 1.2 and 2.3. Also relevant: a submodule PR cannot be verified in its own repo, since coverage.sh, the configs and the baselines all live in the superproject -- so whatever gate is chosen, the submodule review is the last one that can still stop the work, and submodule merges are irreversible in practice.
acceptance_criteria: A recorded decision naming the review artifact and the superproject's gate, with the submodule protection applied if that is the outcome.

title: Correct the /coverage-loop exit path: re-attach, stage ledgers, carry evidence
description:
Four corrections to the exit path in .claude/commands/coverage-loop.md.

Re-attach the submodules. Recording a pointer leaves each submodule detached at the merge sha, which is correct for the bump and wrong as a resting state -- Stage 0 step 2 refuses to start when any submodule is detached, so the success path is the next run's blocked preflight. Re-attach with git switch <default> and git pull --ff-only, and do it after the superproject PR merges, not after the bump: until then the default branch is not yet where the pointer says it is.

Stage the triage ledgers with the baselines. Step 3 mentions only baseline files. The ledger is the evidence for what the run decided not to test, and it belongs in the same commit as the ratchet advance -- otherwise it stays modified and the superproject preflight fails.

Carry the evidence in the PR body, not as a path. Step 2 relies on reviewers seeing the loop log, but .claude/artifacts/loop-log.json is gitignored and does not exist in the submodule repos at all -- a reviewer opening a helios PR gets a pointer to an uncommitted file in a different repository. Paste the iteration's loop-log entry and the verifier findings into the body. Say plainly why, too: a submodule PR reviewer cannot run the gate, because coverage.sh, the configs and the baselines all live in the superproject. The verifier report is the only evidence that PR carries.

Handle zero submodule merges. The gate rewrites the superproject baselines and ledgers on every run, so zero submodule merges does not mean nothing to ship -- it means ship the superproject alone, or discard the measurement and say so. As written the run ends with a dirty superproject tree and an uncommitted ratchet advance.
design: Sources: harness-build-instructions-review.md sections 4.3, 1.2, 5.2 and 5.3; ship-harness-audit.md sections 4.4, 4.6, 5.1 and 5.4. The re-attach item pairs with the detached-HEAD guard bug -- with that fixed the failure at least becomes loud instead of silent.
acceptance_criteria: After a full run, no submodule is left detached. The superproject tree is clean. A submodule PR body contains the verifier findings and the iteration's numbers rather than a path to them.

title: Fix /coverage-loop Stage 0 preflight: generated files and pre-existing branches
description:
Two preflight defects that fire on the loop's own output.

Dirty-tree check (coverage-loop.md lines 29-32). Stage 2 rewrites coverage/*.triage.json every iteration and those files are tracked, so a resumed run's preflight trips on work the loop itself did. Separately, default git status --porcelain reports a submodule as modified for untracked content inside it, so one stray .DS_Store in helios fails the preflight as dirty tree with no indication which repo caused it. Fix: check with --ignore-submodules=untracked, and treat coverage/*.triage.json and coverage/*.baseline.json as expected-generated by name -- anything else dirty still stops the run.

Pre-existing branch (step 3). Nothing in the harness deletes test/coverage-loop, and the exit path that says to delete it does not. A second run's git switch -c collides with the stale local branch. Fix: if the branch already exists, either resume onto it by reading loop-log, or stop and say so -- and make the exit path actually perform the deletes, local and remote.

## Steps to Reproduce

Generated files: run ./tools/triage.sh, then git status --porcelain in the superproject. coverage/*.triage.json show as modified, so Stage 0 step 1 stops the run.

Untracked content: touch helios/.DS_Store, then git status --porcelain in the superproject. helios reports as modified, so Stage 0 step 1 stops the run naming the superproject rather than helios.

Stale branch: run /coverage-loop to any stop condition, then run it again. Stage 0 step 3 git switch -c test/coverage-loop fails because the branch already exists.
design: Sources: harness-build-instructions-review.md section 1.2, ship-harness-audit.md sections 4.6 and 5.2. Verified: coverage/*.triage.json are tracked in the superproject and no submodule.*.ignore is configured.
acceptance_criteria: A second consecutive /coverage-loop run passes Stage 0 without manual cleanup. A .DS_Store inside a submodule does not read as a dirty superproject.

title: Make the verifier's read-only restraint checkable instead of claimed
description:
verifier.md line 8 says: You have no edit tools, so you cannot quietly fix what you find. That is false. The verifier has Bash, and sed -i, shell redirection and git commit are all Bash. coverage-runner.md lines 8-11 make the same claim. What exists today is instruction-backed restraint dressed as structural enforcement, which matters most for the verifier: a reviewer that can quietly fix what it finds and is merely told not to is back in grading-its-own-work territory.

Three changes:

1. Give the restraint teeth without per-agent tool policing. The orchestrator fingerprints the submodule around the verifier's turn -- git rev-parse HEAD plus a hash of git status --porcelain, taken immediately before dispatch and asserted identical after. That catches mutation by any route and costs two Bash calls. Add the corresponding line to verifier.md so the agent knows the check exists.

2. Replace the false sentences in verifier.md and coverage-runner.md with the true weaker ones.

3. Route the verifier through a different model. Change its frontmatter from sonnet to opus, leaving the authoring agents on sonnet. Fresh context protects against motivated error; a different model is the only cheap lever against correlated error, where author and reviewer share a blind spot.
design: The fingerprint approach was chosen over a PreToolUse hook keyed on agent identity because it is not established that the PreToolUse payload carries subagent identity -- unverified, and the fingerprint does not depend on knowing. Sources: refinements/doctrine-errors.md points 1 and 2.
acceptance_criteria: No file in .claude/agents claims an agent cannot edit when it holds Bash. A verifier that mutated the tree is detected by the orchestrator, not by its own report. The verifier runs on a different model from the authors.

title: guard-default-branch.py allows a commit made from a detached HEAD
description:
In .claude/hooks/guard-default-branch.py, git() returns None when a git call fails. In a detached working tree git symbolic-ref --short HEAD fails, so branch is None, the comparison at line 109 against protected is False, and the commit is allowed.

CLAUDE.md forbids committing from a detached submodule HEAD, and this is the one hook meant to enforce branch policy. It is blind to exactly that state today -- independent of any future ship harness.

Fix: distinguish detached from on-a-branch. If symbolic-ref --short HEAD fails but rev-parse --verify HEAD succeeds, the repo is real and simply detached -- refuse with a message naming the repo and telling the caller to git switch to a branch first.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. git -C helios checkout --detach HEAD
2. Touch any file in helios and stage it.
3. Ask the agent to run git -C helios commit -m wip.
4. The PreToolUse guard allows it. Expected: refused, per the CLAUDE.md rule against committing from a detached submodule HEAD.
5. Restore with git -C helios switch master.
design: About six lines around line 108-116. Note the fallback path in default_branch() is fine as things stand -- verified that origin/HEAD is set in the superproject and all three submodules, so the guard is not silently no-oping for that reason. Source: refinements/ship-harness-audit.md section 4.4, corroborated by harness-build-instructions-review.md section 4.3.
acceptance_criteria: A git commit attempted from a detached submodule HEAD is refused with a message that names the repo.

title: Give the hooks a heartbeat so fail-open is distinguishable from dead
description:
Both hooks fail open on their own bugs, which is the right per-invocation choice, but nothing in the design ever confirms they are alive. A guard that fails open on a broken config fails open forever, silently, and no artifact would show it.

Have guard-default-branch.py and check-test-syntax.py each append one line to .claude/artifacts/hook-log.jsonl on every invocation, including the ones that pass: hook name, decision (allow / refuse / skip), and reason. Then have /coverage-loop Stage 5 fold the counts into the loop-log entry as a guards field.

.claude/artifacts/ is already gitignored, so this does not touch any tree the gate inspects.
design: Roughly four lines per hook. Fail-open is defensible only when liveness is observable; without this it is a smoke detector with no low-battery chirp. Source: refinements/doctrine-errors.md point 3.
acceptance_criteria: Every hook invocation appends a line. A loop-log entry reports how many times each guard fired and with what decision.

title: Move selection and ordering judgment from the triager agent into the triage skill
description:
Churn weighting, blocker grouping and disjoint test-file assignment live in .claude/agents/triager.md lines 27-38. That is the highest-stakes judgment in the pipeline -- it sets what gets worked on -- and by the harness's own layering rule (skills are the judgment, agents are the isolation) it is in the wrong file.

Move that section verbatim into .claude/skills/triage/SKILL.md under a Selection and ordering heading. Leave the agent with only the artifact contract, the ?-bucket mechanic, and the report format.

One reframe is needed on the way across: Disjointness is written for the loop's parallel writers, so it needs a conditional opener along the lines of when the work will be split across authors, so it reads correctly for someone invoking the skill standalone.
design: Two payoffs. Asking what should we test next outside the loop currently gets a poorer answer than the loop gets, because the ranking rules are invisible to the skill. And judgment parked in an agent is untouched by any skill-level evaluation. Source: refinements/doctrine-errors.md point 7.
acceptance_criteria: triager.md contains no ranking heuristics. The triage skill produces the same ordering standalone that the loop produces.

title: coverage.sh hides build errors behind the gate-failure exit code
description: tools/coverage.sh returns 2 from run_one for a compile, link or config error, but the top level only does 'exit 1' when FAILED is non-empty. A caller therefore cannot tell a build error from a coverage regression without parsing stderr, which is exactly what .claude/skills/coverage/SKILL.md and the coverage-runner agent claim the exit code does ('1 is the gate failing, 2 is a configuration or build error'). Propagate the worst per-submodule status to the top-level exit instead.
acceptance_criteria: A submodule that fails to compile makes the script exit 2; a submodule that regresses below baseline makes it exit 1; a run with both exits 2.

title: Trim the coverage and triage skills to judgment only
description: Both SKILL.md files carry copies of data that lives authoritatively elsewhere, and both have already gone stale: coverage/SKILL.md says helios includes Helios.cpp (its config's _scope says the opposite), and triage/SKILL.md's Current state table predates the re-scope. Delete the derived content (flag tables duplicating --help, the scope paragraph duplicating _scope, the current-state tables duplicating the ledger) and keep only what a script cannot carry: the C-bucket argument, the calibration limits, the reporting guidance. Move the scope/baseline prohibitions into the scripts' failure output, since a skill is only loaded when the model chooses to load it and the guardrail is needed precisely when nobody asked.

title: Enforce the branch policy mechanically
description: Nothing currently prevents a commit on a default branch: .claude/settings.json has empty hooks, settings.local.json pre-approves 'git commit -m *' and 'git push *' with no branch guard, and there is no .github/ or CODEOWNERS in any of the four repos. Add a PreToolUse hook that refuses a commit or push when HEAD is the default branch, plus GitHub branch protection.
notes: Hook half done on feat/coverage-loop: .claude/hooks/guard-default-branch.py refuses a commit on a default branch and a push whose explicit destination is one, in the superproject and the submodules, reading origin/HEAD rather than assuming a name. Still open: GitHub branch protection on all four repos, which is the half a local hook cannot provide.

title: Redo the helios Metal port under the new process
description: The deleted fork carried a Metal port (v2.2.0, v2.2.1, and the origin/modernize branch) that is not on the re-forked remote and is not recoverable locally — there is no .git/modules/helios. Rebuild it from v2.1.1 as a series of feat/<topic> branches and PRs against helios master, then bump the superproject pointer in a separate PR.

title: Audit triage verdict precision on all three submodules
description: Run triage across helios, hills and hyperspace and hand-audit a sample of verdicts per submodule, with attention to the C bucket where a wrong verdict silently removes work from the queue. If the unknown rate is above roughly a third, the clang AST path stops being a contingency and becomes a requirement for the classifier.
close_reason: audited: 12/12 C and 10/10 A verdicts correct by hand-check; unknown rate 1/241 helios, 0/16 hills, 1/214 hyperspace -- far under the one-third bar, so the clang AST path stays a contingency. One false positive found and removed (c:dead-port misread a #else arm as dead)

title: Add triage front door: tools/triage.sh and the triage skill
description: tools/triage.sh drives the region export plus the classifier and prints the per-submodule verdict; .claude/skills/triage/SKILL.md is the front door, mirroring the coverage skill's discipline that the script is the logic. The skill must state that 100% is the wrong target, report the addressable ceiling, and forbid triage from editing coverage config scope.
close_reason: tools/triage.sh + .claude/skills/triage/SKILL.md landed; coverage skill cross-references it

title: Build triage classifier (rules + ledger)
description: tools/triage_classify.py turns the region export into A/B/C verdicts using a fixed-precedence deterministic rule table, writing coverage/<name>.triage.json keyed on path::signature. Anything the rules cannot decide is marked unknown and escalated to human/model judgment, which is then persisted so it is not re-litigated each run.
close_reason: classifier + ledger landed; rule table validated on all three submodules, 12/12 C and 10/10 A verdicts correct on hand-audit, dead-port rule removed as unfixable

title: Add --regions export to coverage.sh (null-driver path)
description: Triage needs llvm-cov's per-function region data, including when a submodule has no test drivers yet. Extend tools/coverage.sh with --regions FILE: synthesize a stub main when tests/ is empty, and run a full llvm-cov export instead of -summary-only. Reuses the existing config resolution, per-extension compile rules and framework linking so triage and the gate share one build path and one denominator.
close_reason: coverage.sh --regions lands with the null-driver path; verified on all three submodules (helios 241, hyperspace 214, hills 16 functions enumerated at 0%)

title: Write test drivers to arm the coverage gate
description: The coverage gate runs but reports 0% because no submodule has a tests/ directory. Add drivers under helios/tests, hyperspace/tests, hills/tests. Start with preference loading/clamping (proven crash source), then characterization tests on Implicit and rsMath before hyperspace is ported.
notes: The harness convention is now specified in .claude/skills/testing/SKILL.md: tests/harness.h registers cases with __attribute__((constructor)) so C, C++ and Objective-C sources can all include it; tests/main.cpp is the single main() the whole submodule links against; topic files are tests/test_<topic>.cpp with no main. Building that harness is the first commit in any submodule, and /coverage-loop stage 0 blocks until it exists.

title: Coverage gate: tools/coverage.sh + /coverage skill
description: Ratchet-based code coverage gate for each submodule. Scope is the testable C++/ObjC core (AppKit/Metal excluded and documented). Built on clang -fprofile-instr-generate + llvm-cov export, not xcodebuild/xccov, because xcodebuild -list exits 70 on this machine (IDESimulatorFoundation plugin failure) and no .xcscheme files exist in any repo. Script lives in each submodule so their CI can run it standalone; parent holds the skill.

title: Add helios, hills, hyperspace as git submodules
description: The three screen saver projects are nested git repos sitting untracked in the parent repo. Register them as proper submodules pointing at their GitHub origins so the parent repo records pinned commits instead of ignoring them.

title: Narrow the gh pr permission so merging is a deliberate act
description:
.claude/settings.local.json pre-approves Bash(gh pr *), which includes gh pr merge. Meanwhile no repo in the project has any server-side review gate today -- verified in both audits: no .github/workflows anywhere, no branch protection, and the already-merged screen-savers PR #3 shows empty statusCheckRollup, reviewDecision and latestReviews. So the freehand merge path is wide open in a design that treats independent review as load-bearing.

Narrow the allow entry to the read and create verbs, or add Bash(gh pr merge:*) to permissions.deny in settings.json, which takes precedence.

State the limit honestly when doing it: this constrains only the hand-typed path. A merge performed inside a script is invisible to the permission layer, the same blindness that makes the proposed gh pr merge hook clause unable to fire. This is honest friction, not a gate.
design: Low priority precisely because of that limit -- it is worth doing, but it should not be mistaken for the review gate the superproject still lacks.
acceptance_criteria: gh pr merge prompts for approval rather than running pre-approved.

title: Record the decision not to add a gh pr merge clause to guard-default-branch.py
description:
The harness build instructions propose adding a clause to guard-default-branch.py that blocks gh pr merge when the tree is dirty or the head branch has unpushed commits. Two independent audits reached the same conclusion: it cannot fire, and the effort belongs elsewhere.

Why it cannot fire. The PreToolUse hook matches Bash and reads tool_input.command. Any gh pr merge run by a ship script executes inside that script, so the hook sees ./tools/ship.sh helios and nothing more. It would only ever catch a hand-typed gh pr merge -- the exact thing the harness design says the orchestrator has stopped doing. It is also not a clause: parse() yields only invocations whose argv[0] basename is git, so this would be a structural rewrite of the hook. And the dirty-tree and unpushed-commit checks would inspect the wrong repository, since the hook resolves cwd from the payload while a ship script cds into the submodule internally.

Why it is unnecessary anyway. The case it targets -- merging a PR that does not contain what is on disk -- cannot arise in a script that pushes before it polls. The genuinely new risk a ship harness introduces is merging before review, and a PreToolUse hook cannot see that either.

Write the decision down where the hook lives so it is not re-proposed.
design: Sources: ship-harness-audit.md section 7 and harness-build-instructions-review.md section 6, reached independently. The recommended alternative -- asserting branch protection at preflight -- is tracked separately as the superproject review-gate decision.
acceptance_criteria: A comment or note in the hook or its docs states the clause was evaluated and rejected, with the reason.

title: Give the closed C-set an amendment process
description:
The triage skill closes the C reason set -- c:compiler-generated, c:trivial-accessor, c:generated-table, c:vendored-unmodified -- which is right, since an open-ended not worth it becomes a place to put anything inconvenient. But lines 58-60 say a new reason is discussed, not a one-off without naming a venue. A constitution with no amendment clause fails a particular way: legitimate new categories accumulate in the ? bucket, resolved one verdict at a time, and the pressure to misfile into an existing C grows.

The evidence an amendment needs is already being collected -- human --set verdicts keep rule_would_say when they disagree with the rules. Write the clause into the skill: when three or more human verdicts share a rationale no existing rule captures, that is a proposal for a new closed-set member, filed as a pull request against the rule table in tools/triage_classify.py citing those ledger entries as evidence.

The same paragraph should name where the doctrine itself gets amended. It is currently stated across five files with no designated seat, so a principle that loses an argument with reality has nowhere to be revised.
acceptance_criteria: The triage skill names a threshold, a venue and an evidence source for adding a C reason.

title: Derive the loop's stop decision from loop-log rather than a fixed cap
description:
Two related gaps in Stage 5's decision table.

The hard cap of 3 iterations is fixed by impression, in prose, forever -- in a design whose stated reason for keeping loop-log is that is this working gets answered with data rather than impression. A loop still improving at iteration 3 stops; one that plateaued at 2 already wasted an iteration. Replace the addressable did not improve row with a marginal-gain floor read from loop-log -- stop when the iteration's addressable gain falls below a floor -- and keep 3 as the outer bound rather than the rule. The log already records addressable per iteration; the data is there and simply unused.

Escalation is only a success if escalations get consumed. The loop files a bd issue per blocked entry but models no human capacity, so it has no answer to a backlog of successful escalations nobody reads. Add to Stage 0: if open escalation issues from prior runs exceed a threshold, stop and report -- another run would add to a pile rather than to coverage.
design: Source: refinements/doctrine-errors.md point 5. The point is self-application: a system built on answer with data has not turned that principle on its own stop rule.
acceptance_criteria: The stop decision reads a number out of loop-log. Stage 0 refuses to start on an unconsumed escalation backlog.

title: Unblock parallel test-writers within a single submodule
description: /coverage-loop serializes test-writer dispatch within one submodule because the agents share one working tree and one git index, and because tools/coverage.sh hardcodes BUILD_ROOT=.coverage-build and does 'rm -rf' on it at the start of every build. Two concurrent gate runs against the same submodule destroy each other. Unblocking it needs two changes: a COVERAGE_BUILD_ROOT (or --build-dir) override in coverage.sh, and a per-writer git worktree of the submodule so drafts do not collide. Only worth doing if wall-clock in the loop turns out to matter.
design: Cross-submodule parallelism already works and is what the loop uses today; this is about the within-submodule case.

title: Decide hyperspace impCubeVolume::polygonize triage verdict
description: The classifier cannot isolate polygonize's body because #if USE_TRIANGLE_STRIPS splits the loop across preprocessor arms, so it sits in the ? bucket awaiting a human call. The identical function in helios was judged A. Record with: tools/triage.sh hyperspace --set 'impCubeVolume::polygonize(unsigned int)' --verdict A --reason '...'
